_meta.description: Document-rules config for divorce_sma — contested divorce under Special Marriage Act, 1954

title: Petition for Divorce under Special Marriage Act, 1954

fields.label: Petitioner religion (for record only — SMA is religion-neutral)
Place of marriage / SMA registration office
Narrative of facts grounding the petition
Proof of 3-year residence (if basis = petitioner residence)

fields.name: Express denial of collusion / connivance (S.34 SMA)

mandatory_clauses.name: SMA Marriage Solemnisation
mandatory_clauses.description: Pleading that marriage was solemnised / registered under Special Marriage Act, 1954 with certificate particulars

mandatory_clauses.name: Jurisdiction u/s 31 SMA
mandatory_clauses.description: Note: three-year residence rule where petitioner relies on own residence

verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {petitioner_name}, aged about {petitioner_age} years, resident of {petitioner_address}, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above petition are true and correct to the best of my knowledge derived from records and personal experience. Paragraphs containing legal submissions are believed true on advice of counsel. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Petitioner

promptInstructions: Draft a contested divorce petition under Section 27 of the Special Marriage Act, 1954.
Open with averments of valid SMA marriage — date, place, certificate number/date, Registrar of Marriages.
SMA is a secular statute; do NOT invoke Hindu/Muslim/Christian personal law. Useful for inter-faith marriages and civil registrations.
Plead specific S.27 ground(s) with cogent particulars (adultery / desertion 2 years / imprisonment 7+ years / cruelty / mental disorder / communicable venereal disease / presumption of death).

S.27(1A) — additional grounds for wife: rape/sodomy/bestiality post-marriage; decree for maintenance under S.125 CrPC / S.144 BNSS / S.18 Hindu Adoption & Maintenance Act subsisting and parties not living together for one year+.
Include S.34(1) mandatory averments: no collusion / connivance, no condonation, no improper delay.

Establish jurisdiction under S.31 SMA. Note: if relying on petitioner's residence and respondent resides outside territory, petitioner must have resided there for THREE years immediately preceding petition.
Use formal, respectful language. SMA marriages are religion-neutral; do not assume Hindu identity.
Do NOT generate verification or signature blocks — added programmatically.

sections.description: Grounds for divorce available to either spouse
Desertion for continuous period of not less than two years
Imprisonment for 7+ years for offence under IPC/BNS
Incurable unsoundness of mind / continuous or intermittent mental disorder
Presumption of death — not heard of for 7 years
Jurisdiction — three-year residence rule where petitioner relies on own residence
Duty of court — collusion, condonation, delay, taking advantage of own wrong

filing_checklist: Certified copy of SMA marriage certificate
Documents evidencing grounds (medical / police / witness affidavits)
Proof of 3-year residence if jurisdiction relies on petitioner residence
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: petitioner_name and respondent_name must not be empty
marriage_date must precede filing_date by at least 1 year (S.29 SMA bar against divorce within 1 year)
grounds_selected must contain at least one ground
If jurisdiction_basis = 'where_petitioner_resides_three_years', three_year_residence_proof must not be empty
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format
key_citations: Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2000) 6 SCC 224 — significance of SMA for inter-faith marriages
Samar Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh (2007) 4 SCC 511 — cruelty principles equally applied under SMA
Sarla Mudgal v. Union of India (1995) 3 SCC 635 — conversion and SMA
disclaimer: Lawie is a drafting assistant. The advocate is responsible for legal accuracy and filing.
